title: the search parties
hook: a ring with Rama's name, and three parties come home empty-handed

segments.voice: Yesterday: the search parties set out, four directions, a map learned by running, and one month. Today the week closes.

Before the southern party leaves, Rama calls Hanuman aside. Of all the leaders and all the armies, it's Hanuman he picks out. Sugriva's confidence in him is obvious, and Rama has his own reasons, going back to that first conversation on Rishyamuka, the sentence with not one word wrong. He takes something small off his finger and holds it out. It's the kind of thing you'd give someone only if you were sure of them.
screen: `RAMA CALLS HANUMAN ASIDE.` → `SOMETHING SMALL, HELD OUT.`

segments.voice: It's a ring, engraved with Rama's name. Take this, Rama tells him, so that when you find her, she'll know you come from me, and won't be afraid. Hanuman will meet Sita as a stranger, a monkey in an enemy city. Words alone might not be believed. A ring she knows will be. Rama is planning ahead for the moment when trust will matter most. And why Hanuman? Valmiki gives the reason: Sugriva is surest of him, and Rama sees his resolve and believes this one will succeed. Hanuman takes the ring, raises it to his head with joined palms, and bows at Rama's feet before he sets out. Then the month passes. The parties to the east, the west and the north search everything Sugriva described: mountains, forests, caves, rivers, cities. They come back on time, and they come back with nothing. No sign of Sita. Now everyone is waiting on the south. The week, from the top. The monsoon poem, the sky giving birth to rain. Hanuman's early reminder, and a clear autumn sky. Rama's message: the path Vali took is not closed. Lakshmana's bowstring, and Tara's calm. Sugriva's apology, and armies covering the earth. Four directions and a map learned by running. And today, a ring, and three empty-handed returns.
screen: `A RING WITH RAMA'S NAME.` · `WHY HANUMAN.` · `THREE PARTIES RETURN EMPTY.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `EVERYONE WAITS ON THE SOUTH.`

segments.voice: If you're wearing a ring or something small you value, rest your attention on it; if not, picture something small that someone once gave you. Breathe in and remember who gave it; breathe out and feel what it carries: their trust, their memory, their hope.
Anguliya, a finger-ring: the one Rama gives Hanuman today, engraved with his name, so Sita will know he sent him.
Your line: everyone waits on the south. One small ring carries a lot of hope. Day five hundred ninety-five, done.

screen: `DAY 595 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK FROM THE RAINS TO THE RING, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: THE CAVE OF SVAYAMPRABHA.`

howItsDone: In paintings and temple carvings, Hanuman is often shown kneeling before Sita and holding out Rama's ring, the moment this token was given for.

chat.says: Why did Rama give Hanuman his ring before the search began?
options: So Sita would know he truly came from Rama, and not be afraid of a stranger.
To pay Hanuman ahead of time for leading the southern search party.
So Hanuman could trade it for a ship to carry him across to Lanka.
chat.meaning: The ring, engraved with Rama's name, is a token: Hanuman will meet Sita as a stranger, and a ring she knows will be believed.
